title: Active Record Core
intro: Active Record is the ORM at the heart of every Rails application, and the questions interviewers ask about it reveal whether a candidate understands it as a tool or as a black box. This page covers the Active Record pattern (vs Data Mapper), the full CRUD API and bang method semantics, validations (presence, uniqueness, custom validator objects, and validation contexts), the callback execution order (before_validation through after_commit) and the critical gotcha that after_save fires inside the transaction while after_commit fires after it (use after_commit for external side effects), named scopes vs class methods, the default_scope danger, optimistic locking with :lock_version, and pessimistic locking with with_lock.
